$comment: Paired measurements: the SAME quantity on the SAME face, measured by TrueMax
and read off a competitor's own UI. Nothing here is their code, model or
formula — every `theirs` value is a number their product displayed to a
paying user, which is what any customer can read off the screen.
This file exists to answer ONE question: does our pipeline measure the same
thing they do, and if not, is our disagreement systematic. It is deliberately
NOT a calibration set. Fitting anything to their SCORES would be reverse-
engineering their scoring by regression, which is the thing we said we would
not do, merely done statistically instead of by reading code. Their scores are
recorded for context and are never a target.
Add a face by appending to `faces`. Rows only need `ours` and `theirs` in the
SAME units — convert on the way in and say so in `note`. Run:

faces.name: Justin Bieber
note: Their Harmony pillar splits by view, which Cavill's capture did not show, and it is the
most useful number either product has produced so far: front 5.33 against side 8.23 on
one face. Our merged overall is 5.5 with the side at 6.8, so our front sits BELOW 5.5 —
the results screen does display a front-only figure but it was not in the capture, so it
is recorded as unknown rather than inferred. Read the front comparison only once that
No paired metric rows yet: their per-card values were not captured, only the pillar
figures and the qualitative strength/improvement lists, which are deviations rather than
measurements and cannot be paired against ours.

theirCards.card: Total Facial Width to Height Ratio
Lower Lip to Upper Lip Ratio
Mouth width to nose width ratio

cardNote: Their ideal bands and axis ranges on these five cards are IDENTICAL to the same cards on
the Cavill capture — Top Third 30.0-32.0 over 19.8-42.2, Lower Third 33.9-37.0 over
So their bands are per-metric CONSTANTS, not per-person, and a further face adds no
information about band width at all. Two male faces only; a female capture would say
Only one row here is safely pairable against ours. Their Total Facial W:H is described
on the card as height-to-width, which is our facialIndex — 1.40 against our 1.38. The
thirds are NOT pairable as they stand: their thirds are shares of trichion-to-menton
while our lowerFacePct is a share of glabella-to-menton, so 38.0 against our 50.5 is two
different quantities rather than a disagreement. Their Midface Ratio is interpupillary
against midface height, which is our midfaceRatio and not our middleLowerBalance — the
value for it was not in the capture.
Completing this needs the TrueMax diagnostics dump, which names every metric, rather than
region cards read off a screenshot.

their Jaw Slope; agreement to 0.2 degrees, the closest pairing recorded so far

note: HELD AS UNCONFIRMED. Their card draws what looks like the same construction — a V at
the chin subtended by the two jaw corners — but 114.1 against 87.9 is a 30% gap, far
larger than any other pairing here, and a difference that size is more often two
definitions than one disagreement. Their ideal band is 86.5-92.5, which our value could
not reach under any placement, so if the definitions DO match this is either a real
measurement fault of ours or an ideal in the wrong place. Worth resolving directly
rather than averaging into a bias estimate: excluded from the audit until then.
